text:
elaine: Quick notes from today's topic-aware verifier experiment. Idea: run a tiny classifier on the prompt to predict "risk" (factual/long-context/code) and pick verifier thresholds dynamically rather than a single early_abort. Ran on ember-13b-q4h with spec_predictor=greedy, verifier=greedy, and per-topic thresholds. Observed ~1.85x token throughput and p50 ~1.5x improvement. Quality: overall ROUGE-L ~0.7pt down but for "high-risk" bucket the ROUGE/BERTScore delta reduced to ~0.1pt vs baseline.

david: nice. what classifier and labels?

elaine: lightweight SVM on token-features + heuristic tagger: labels=[low,medium,high]. High = code + knowledge QA + longform>800 tokens. Classifier accuracy ~88% on dev. We used early_abort: low=0.02, medium=0.06, high=0.14 (more conservative for high risk). Also turned off kv_prefetch for high-risk to reduce mis-prefetch effects.

nora: can you paste the eval command and the routing pseudo-config?

elaine: command:
```
./eval_harness \\
  --model ember-13b-q4h \\
  --speculative=greedy \\
  --topic_classifier=svc_small \\
  --early_abort_policy="low:0.02,medium:0.06,high:0.14" \\
  --kv_prefetch_policy="high:false,else:true" \\
  --tasks=summarization,code,qa \\
  --holdout=topic-aware-holdout-v1 \\
  --batch=10
```

elaine: metrics: spec_confidence_gap (verifier_score - predictor_score), accept_rate_by_topic, and per-topic ROUGE/BLEU/BERTScore recorded. High-risk accept_rate ~56%, low-risk ~82%.

david: interesting metric spec_confidence_gap. Did you see systematic shifts by quant profile?

elaine: yes, q4h shifts verifier raw scores higher, so naive thresholds would accept too much. We calibrated thresholds on dev via temperature scaling per-quant profile. Without calibration high-risk accept_rate would be ~70% and regressions spike.

nora: any regression significance?

elaine: ran paired-bootstrap on ROUGE-L n=2000: overall p~0.11 (not significant), high-risk cohort p~0.42 (no regression vs baseline), low-risk p~0.06 (small non-sig drop). So adaptive routing seems to protect risky inputs while keeping performance gains.

david: what's overhead of the classifier? It needs to be tiny or it kills latency gains.

elaine: classifier is ~3ms median on CPU; we batch classify per-request quickly in the runtime pre-hook. Net p50 still improved. We also cached topic tags for identical user sessions to avoid repeat cost.

nora: cool. next steps?

elaine: (1) run fuller sweep with alternative thresholds and with/without kv_prefetch for medium; (2) add per-case logging for cases where verifier accepted but final edit increased tokens significantly (possible truncation); (3) try cross-model verifier for high-risk only (cheap small-verifier ensemble before calling big model). I'll push branch `exp/topic-aware-verifier-766789` and queue CI.
